WV13-P01.5.note: A scale that is whistled up and down is a series of musical notes; the engine needing no water rules out a boiler-scale crust.

exclusions.A: The council should put the first train back at dawn, load the cheese, and give the visitors the second train, which would still reach Gessen in good light for their photographs.
exclusions.B: The farmers are the ones who lose by the change.
exclusions.C: A line built to serve the village's farmers now runs at the hours that suit the hotels, and the farmers are left to hire trucks.
exclusions.E: In winter, when the visitors stay away, the trains stand in the shed at Pell, and the snowploughs keep the road open for everything else.

support: None of this needed to happen.
The council should put the first train back at dawn, load the cheese, and give the visitors the second train, which would still reach Gessen in good light for their photographs.
WV13-P01.6.note: The author faults the council's timetable for abandoning the farmers the line was built to serve and prescribes a fix, which is criticism rather than longing, amusement, admiration or fear.

exclusions.A: By three o'clock the terrace was half empty, because the café's glass walls throw a long shadow across it.
exclusions.B: The pike belongs under the water, and the café belongs at the gate.
exclusions.C: The café should have gone by the north gate, where its shadow would have fallen on the car park.
exclusions.E: Putting a glass box on the sunny end of a west-facing terrace was the wrong decision, made for the sake of the café's takings.

support: Putting a glass box on the sunny end of a west-facing terrace was the wrong decision, made for the sake of the café's takings.
The café should have gone by the north gate, where its shadow would have fallen on the car park.
WV13-P02.5.note: The writer judges the cafe's placement a wrong decision and states where it should have gone, a confident disapproval with no expressed sorrow, unease or humour.

exclusions.A: What the bridges needed this summer was repair, not paint.
exclusions.C: Those repairs, already logged by the inspectors, were put off to next year, and the parks crew's orders were to paint straight over the chalk.
exclusions.D: For fifty years before this summer, the seven footbridges over the Askel were the colour of wet pavement.
exclusions.E: The city should have mended the railings in the spring and painted the bridges next year, in whatever colours its residents and its schoolchildren chose.

support: What the bridges needed this summer was repair, not paint.
Instead it has put a bright coat over eleven red rings and called the job finished.
WV13-P03.5.note: The writer objects that paint was put ahead of logged repairs and the residents' wishes; even the dry remark about Varga's interviews, read ironically, still points to disapproval rather than amusement.

exclusions.A: The committee should have kept the Knuckle compulsory for every rider and given newcomers a shorter course of their own.
exclusions.C: He passed Arlo outside the old chapel, swung onto the track while Arlo hauled himself up the cobbles, and came past the war memorial alone to reach the green in 9:52, a winning time well outside the champion's record.
exclusions.D: A hill climb that lets riders go around its hardest bend fails to test the one thing it exists to test.
exclusions.E: This year the committee changed the one rule: to make the climb less daunting for newcomers, riders could take Pell's farm track around the Knuckle.

support: A hill climb that lets riders go around its hardest bend fails to test the one thing it exists to test.
Instead it has made Kesterby's one real test optional, and a test that riders may skip measures nothing.
WV13-P04.5.note: The author argues the rule change makes the climb measure nothing and says what the committee should have done, which is critical rather than admiring, worried, amused or wistful.
